# glinet_client_speed_limit (Resource)

Manages the speed limit of a client device, as the clients page of the web UI does. The write was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. The web UI shows the speed limit only when the router is in router mode or passthrough mode. The web UI does not let you set a limit while network acceleration is on, and says that network acceleration can stop the limits. The resource does not change network acceleration and does not check it. Create fails when the client list of the router has no client with the MAC address, because it is not known whether the router accepts a limit for a MAC address that is not in the list. Create also fails when the client already has a limit. At least one of `download` and `upload` must be more than 0, because it is not known what the router does with two 0 values. When the client goes out of the client list, or has no limit, refresh removes the resource from the state. The provider finds the client without letter case and writes the MAC address in the letter case of the client list. Import sets `mac` in the letter case of the client list. Destroy removes the speed limit from the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Download at most 1024 KiB/s, no upload limit.
resource "glinet_client_speed_limit" "tablet" {
  mac      = "02:00:00:00:00:01"
  download = 1024
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mac` (String) MAC address of the client, in lower case or upper case, for example `02:00:00:00:00:01`. A change of only the letter case changes only the state. Another change replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `download` (Number) Download limit of the client (`limit_rx` of the client list), in KiB/s (the web UI shows KB/s with a base of 1024): 0 for no limit, or 1 to 1073741824 in steps of 0.125 (the Kbps mode of the web UI sends the Kbps value divided by 8). It is not known whether the router keeps a fraction or rounds it: when the value of the router is not 0 and differs from the configured value by less than 1, the state keeps the configured value. Default 0.
- `upload` (Number) Upload limit of the client (`limit_tx` of the client list), in KiB/s (the web UI shows KB/s with a base of 1024): 0 for no limit, or 1 to 1073741824 in steps of 0.125 (the Kbps mode of the web UI sends the Kbps value divided by 8). It is not known whether the router keeps a fraction or rounds it: when the value of the router is not 0 and differs from the configured value by less than 1, the state keeps the configured value. Default 0.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the MAC address, in lower or upper case.
terraform import glinet_client_speed_limit.tablet 02:00:00:00:00:01
```
